claims.text: Bulk HfNbTaTiZr is typically obtained by casting and annealing.
Bulk HfNbTaTiZr naturally contains microstructural disorder.
Bulk HfNbTaTiZr naturally contains approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Explicitly incorporating intrinsic disorder and oxygen-related defects into transport calculations will significantly improve predictions for bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen interstitials, vacancies, lattice distortions, and chemical short-range-order variations occur in the target HfNbTaTiZr specimens.
Local lattice distortions and chemical disorder modulate electron-scattering paths and electrical conductivity in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Defects increase carrier scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Defects alter phonon mean free paths in HfNbTaTiZr.
Ionized-impurity scattering becomes prominent in HfNbTaTiZr at approximately 0–200 K.
At approximately 300–1200 K, altered lattice vibrations, including Umklapp scattering, dominate transport corrections in HfNbTaTiZr.
The defect-aware model will predict electrical and thermal conductivity more accurately than conventional perfect-crystal models in both specified temperature regimes.
The expected correction relative to conventional models is on the order of several tens of percent.
Standard analytical and ab-initio perfect-crystal predictions show notable deviations from measurements on disordered, oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr.

Existing computational approaches for high-entropy alloys have limitations associated with computational cost, system size, force fields, and representation of effects such as lattice distortion and configurational entropy.
The model is applicable only to bulk HfNbTaTiZr with oxygen near 1 wt.% and within 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The model cannot be extended directly to other alloy systems or oxygen concentrations without modification.
An error reduction of less than 20% relative to conventional ideal-crystal models would falsify the accuracy-improvement hypothesis.
Failure of observed defect structures to correlate with the predicted scattering mechanisms would falsify the proposed mechanism.
